- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 1–2 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias of 3–8% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model often fails to reflect mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 60% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.
- When sentiment is 0.0 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to ignore sentiment signals; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overestimating stability.
